name: Calypso

Each player has their own personal trump suit (one player has Spades, another Hearts, etc.). history.origins: Calypso was invented in Trinidad around the 1940s. It gained international attention in the 1950s following promotion by bridge authority Ely Culbertson who championed it as a potential rival to Contract Bridge.
timeline: 1950s: Promoted internationally, particularly in the UK and USA.
1960s-present: A cult favourite among trick-taking enthusiasts.
history.cultural: Named after the Trinidadian musical tradition. The game reflects Caribbean creativity in card game design.
history.evolution: The personal-trump concept is unique among widely played trick-taking games. Using four 52-card decks gives each player multiple copies of cards in their trump suit.

setup.deck: 4 standard 52-card decks shuffled together (208 cards total).
setup.dealing: Each player receives 13 cards per deal. 4 deals per game.

rules.objective: Score points by winning tricks and building Calypsos (complete trump suit sequences). First partnership to reach target score wins.
rules.gameplay: 1. Deal 13 each (4 decks = 208 cards). 2. Each player has personal trump (one suit). 3. Left of dealer leads. 4. Follow suit or trump. 5. Trump beats non-trump. 6. Build Calypsos (complete A-K of your trump) from won tricks. 7. Surplus trump cards in tricks = 10 pts each at game end. 8. 4 deals; first to target wins.
keyRules: Each player has their own personal trump suit.
Surplus duplicates of trump cards in hand cannot be added to a Calypso â€” only one of each rank needed.
Cards won in tricks that don't contribute to your Calypso are worth 10 pts each at game end.

strategy.basic: Win tricks containing your trump suit cards. Lead from suits your partner is short in to create trump opportunities.
strategy.intermediate: Track which trump ranks you still need. Prioritise winning tricks containing missing Calypso cards over just winning tricks generally.
strategy.advanced: With 4 decks, each trump card appears 4 times â€” but you only need one of each rank. Feed surplus trump cards to partner trick-winners for their 10-pt value. Manage your 13-card hand to maintain coverage across all 4 suits.
tips: Your trump beats ALL non-personal-trump cards â€” use it aggressively when you need a specific rank.
Completing even one Calypso (500 pts) can be decisive.

variations.name: Three-Player Calypso
variations.description: Three players, each with own trump plus one suit shared as common trump. Rare variant.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Rare variant; source does not specify engine parameter overrides for three-player play.

scoring.description: Complete Calypso = 500 (first) or 250 (subsequent). Tricks = 20 each. Partial Calypso cards = 10 each.
scoring.winCondition: Highest score after 4 deals (one full game).

synthesis.shortDescription: The unique Trinidadian trick-taker where every player has their own personal trump suit. Four decks combined. Collect your A through 2 in your trump to complete a Calypso and score 500 big points.
